title: Learning the pattern of epistasis linking genotype and phenotype in a protein
relevance: Comprehensive experimental study of all 2^13 mutants in a fluorescent protein showing extraordinary sparsity of high-order epistasis. Provides the key empirical justification for sparse decomposition approaches.
key_finding: High-order epistatic interactions exist but are extraordinarily sparse, enabling accurate phenotype prediction from limited measurements.

title: Pervasive epistasis exposes intramolecular networks in adaptive enzyme evolution
relevance: Shows that epistasis is pervasive but structurally localized in enzyme evolution. Higher-order epistasis rewires previously established interactions, creating idiosyncrasy. Important caveat for assuming complete pairwise decomposability.
key_finding: Higher-order epistasis causes mutational effects to appear highly idiosyncratic depending on the genetic background.

title: Mega-scale experimental analysis of protein folding stability in biology and design
relevance: 776K experimental stability measurements including double mutants. Quantifies thermodynamic couplings between sites. Provides the data to empirically test the sparsity assumption.
key_finding: Curated set of ~776,000 folding stabilities covering all single amino acid variants and selected double mutants of 479 protein domains.

title: Epistasis shapes the fitness landscape of an allosteric specificity switch
relevance: Demonstrates how epistasis constrains and shapes evolutionary pathways in protein fitness landscapes, relevant to understanding when sparse decomposition is valid.
key_finding: Epistasis between allosteric mutations creates complex fitness landscape topologies that constrain evolutionary paths.
